answer: A mooring bond ties each identity to one canyon beacon post. Each agent posts 70 credits for an ivory tally, key-bound to the beacon's epoch flash; it stamps only when the beacon flashes, never reused. An auditor replays the beacon log: a wrong flash, a rented tally, or a second mooring burns the bond. First costs 42, k-th 42+7(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,538,500 plus 70,000 locked for a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 42 once and keep the bond.
